Tech Report: Best Personal Finance Apps – One App Worth Keeping per Job

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Use one personal finance app for each money job, such as budgeting, spending, investing, and cutting bills, and choose each by its yearly cost and how it makes money.
  • Even a free app that millions used can go away.
  • Each one is the app worth keeping for its job, judged by what it costs a year and what it does that your bank’s own app doesn’t.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Use one personal finance app for each money job, such as budgeting, spending, investing, and cutting bills, and choose each by its yearly cost and how it makes money. A free app still earns money from someone, so learn who pays for it before you link your accounts.

Even a free app that millions used can go away. Intuit shut down Mint, its budgeting app, and invited its users to Credit Karma. So for each pick, this list says whether it makes money from your subscription, from businesses that pay it when you buy or trade, or from an upgrade it sells you.

Each one is the app worth keeping for its job, judged by what it costs a year and what it does that your bank’s own app doesn’t.

Quicken Simplifi builds one spending proposal from every account you link, not just one bank’s, and projects your cash flow. Quicken sells it only as an annual subscription.

For more information, read our full Quicken Simplifi Review.

Recent findings suggest that chime® charges no monthly or overdraft fees, since most of its money comes from a cut of the fee stores pay when you use its card. Round Ups save the change from each purchase.

For more information, read our full Chime Review.

Empower’s dashboard tracks your net worth and retirement blueprint for free, and Empower uses it to offer paid investment advice. You can keep the tracking and turn the advice down.

For more information, read our full Empower Personal Wealth Review.

Robinhood lets you buy stocks and exchange-traded funds in small amounts, with no commission or monthly fee. Trading firms pay it to send them your orders, and it earns income on your idle cash.

For more information, read our full Robinhood Review.

Rocket Money’s free plan lists the subscriptions and recurring bills in your linked accounts. It sells paid aims in which it cancels subscriptions or negotiates bills for you.

For more information, read our full Rocket Money Review.

Brands pay Ibotta a commission only when one of its offers leads to a sale, and they fund the cash back you collect, so the app is free to use.

For more information, read our full Ibotta Review.

Industry observers note that capital One Shopping is free because stores pay it a referral commission when you buy through its links. It’s the shopping tool to keep, since it checks other sellers’ prices as well as coupon codes.

For more information, read our full Capital One Shopping Review.

With Greenlight, kids earn money by finishing chores you set, then spend it with their own debit card, under limits you control. You pay for it with a monthly initiative.

For more information, read our full Greenlight Review.

This list gives each money job one app, along with what it costs and who pays for it. Install the one for the job costing you the most, and add another app only once you’re opening that one every week.

Compare the best budgeting apps to find one that fits how you budget, or the best round-up savings apps to save or invest your spare change.

Australian Grandfather Attempts 1,650Km River Swim

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (334 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that australian grain farm manager Scott Gladman, 63, is attempting to swim the length of the Darling River, Australia’s third-longest river.
  • Gladman started on September 1 from near Brewarrina in far north New South Wales.
  • Sources indicate that interestingly, the expedition is not born from a love of endurance swimming.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that australian grain farm manager Scott Gladman, 63, is attempting to swim the length of the Darling River, Australia’s third-longest river. It begins in New South Wales and finishes at its confluence with the Murray River at Wentworth. Gladman believes he will be the first person to swim the entire 1,650km route.

Gladman started on September 1 from near Brewarrina in far north New South Wales. At the outset, he budgeted 103 days to complete the swim, averaging around 16km per day. So far, he is largely on track. After 49 days, he has covered 660km, leaving just under 1,000km to go.

Sources indicate that interestingly, the expedition is not born from a love of endurance swimming. Gladman was inspired to find a fundraising challenge to support friends impacted by Motor Neuron Disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy, a rare form of Parkinson’s. Initially, he considered the Murray. “I just thought I could swim the Murray River, but people have done that,” he told ABC News. “No one has had a crack at the Darling.”.

It has been revealed that the location of the Darling River in Australia. Photo: Wikimedia Commons.

Gladman gave himself 18 months to train. In the summer, he swam in the Murray River at Boundary Bend, Victoria, and during winter he completed laps in indoor pools. Now out on the Darling, a support boat of family and friends keeps him manufacturer, alongside a canoeist.

“There’s no real form of communication, and I wear earplugs…he’ll [the canoeist] either have to hit me on the back of the head with a paddle to get my attention, or he’ll just start steering toward me, and that will push me one way or the other,” Gladman said.

Despite its length, the Darling River is sometimes so shallow that Gladman needs to float through sections on his back, or walk. The support boat also sometimes requires saving, with Gladman having to help clear a path through river debris:.

#9458. Cashier’s Checks Are Bank-Backed Only When They’re Real – Call the Issuing Bank First

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (493 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Cashier’s Checks Are Bank-Backed Only When They’re Real – Call the Issuing Bank First

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sellers and closing agents ask for cashier’s checks on big payments because the bank’s own money stands behind them, and that trust is why scammers fake them.
  • Deposit one with a teller, and the Federal Reserve’s Regulation CC requires your bank to release the money by the next business day, with a few exceptions, such as holding back part of a large check.
  • Money you can withdraw isn’t proof the check is real.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sellers and closing agents ask for cashier’s checks on big payments because the bank’s own money stands behind them, and that trust is why scammers fake them. Buy yours at your own bank or credit union. When you’re handed one, call the issuing bank at a number you look up yourself before you hand anything over.

Deposit one with a teller, and the Federal Reserve’s Regulation CC requires your bank to release the money by the next business day, with a few exceptions, such as holding back part of a large check. Banks can take weeks to spot a fake, though, and the Federal Trade Commission warns that by then you’re the one who repays the bank.

Money you can withdraw isn’t proof the check is real. Fakes often carry the names of legitimate banks and can fool even bank employees, the FTC says. The bank named on the check is the one that can tell you whether it issued it.

Industry observers note that expect to be asked for one at a home closing, a private car sale, or a lease signing. Buy it at a branch, or online where your bank offers that. You pay the amount up front, plus the fee on your bank’s fee schedule, which some premium checking accounts waive. A certified check is your own check that the bank signs after setting the money aside, and a money order is prepaid too but sold only in small amounts.

According to recent reports, you can stop payment on your own check before it clears, but not on a cashier’s check, which the bank must honor. If one goes missing, you’ll sign a sworn declaration of loss and may have to buy an indemnity bond, insurance that covers the bank if the original gets cashed. The bank can also hold off on a refund or replacement until 90 days after the check’s date.

Anyone paid by cashier’s check should get the issuing bank’s phone number from its own website, never from the check, since the number on a fake may be the scammer’s. The FDIC says the bank will likely ask for the check number, its concern date, and the amount. Turn down a check for more than your asking price, and never send money back out of one you just deposited.

If the issuing bank has no record of the check, don’t deposit it, and report it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

  • Industry observers note that so a number copied from a search may belong to accounts opened in another state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that copy your routing number from your bank’s app or online banking rather than from a web search. Massive banks assign routing numbers by the state where you opened the account and often use a separate one for wires, so confirm which one your payment needs.

It has been revealed that bank of America, for one, ties the routing number to the state where the account was opened, which may not be the state you live in now. Wells Fargo’s routing numbers also depend on that state, and both banks list a separate number for incoming wires.

Industry observers note that so a number copied from a search may belong to accounts opened in another state. The routing number tells a payment which bank to go to, and the account number tells the bank which account is yours. Give the wrong routing number and the payment can bounce back to whoever sent it, which delays your money.

Recent findings suggest that if your account number happens to match another customer’s account at the wrong bank, the money can land there instead. The IRS tells taxpayers whose refund went to the wrong account to work with the bank to get it back.

Sources indicate that in the app or online banking, open the account and look at its details, where the routing number is listed with the account number. On a check, it’s the first number along the bottom, before your account number, and some statements print it too. To confirm that a number is your bank’s, enter it in the American Bankers Association’s lookup, which names the bank it belongs to.

Then match the number to the job:.

For a direct deposit, look in your bank’s app for a form it fills in for you, so both numbers come straight from the bank.

Seven Alpine-Style Climbs Happening Now in Nepal

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, several small teams are attempting difficult climbs on Nepal’s 6,000 and 7,000m peaks.
  • This is what we know about the ongoing expeditions:.
  • Recent findings suggest that three young French climbers, members of the Military High Mountain Group from Chamonix, celebrated their organization’s 50th anniversary with a new route on Peak 41.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, several small teams are attempting difficult climbs on Nepal’s 6,000 and 7,000m peaks. Unfortunately, they rarely report on their plans or progress until they return, and often only if they succeed.

This is what we know about the ongoing expeditions:.

Recent findings suggest that three young French climbers, members of the Military High Mountain Group from Chamonix, celebrated their organization’s 50th anniversary with a new route on Peak 41. This 6,654m mountain is located in the Khumbu region and is often called the “true Mera Peak.”.

According to recent reports, konrad Piontek, Amaury Fouillade, and Clovis Paulin took advantage of a good weather window and achieved the first ascent of the peak’s northeast face. They climbed in an alpine-style single push over four days. The result is a beautiful 1,400m line with difficulties up to ED+ 5+ M6 A1 90°. They descended via the southeast face. The team named their line Bon Matin (good morning).

Nivel Meroi and Romano Benet are acclimatized and ready to attempt a latest route on Jugal II, but the Italian couple will be on their own. Tine Cuder of Slovenia, the third team member, has left due to illness.

Meanwhile, in the Kangchenjunga region, a large Russian team has also finished acclimatizing. The team trekked in the area and crossed a number of high-altitude passes, the latest of them at the top of an icefall at 5,750m. They reported lots of snow above 5,000m but are ready to attempt a new route on the formidable Jannu (7,710m) from its southeast side.

The team comprises Ivan Artemov, Ivan Volkov, Artem Zhdanov, Konstantin Neumoin, Roman Shilin, and Vasily Yagodin.

Hidesuke Taneishi and Tetsu Hashimoto of Japan traveled to Nepal in September, aiming to achieve the first ascent of Gangapurna West (7,455m), also known as Asapurna or Peak Lachenal. They have provided no news since, but they probably had to retreat when an intense snowstorm hit the Annapurna region three weeks ago.

Sources indicate that location of Gangapurna West on a Google Earth screenshot. Notes by Lindsay Griffin for the American Alpine Journal.

Meanwhile, a second team has reached the base of the peak with the same objective. Valery Shamalo, Natalia Zanina, Maksim Trufanov, and Ruslan Kirichenko arrived at the beginning of October and saw no one else there. They reported that recent precipitation had left the trail in a poor state; the climbers had to cross landslides and swollen rivers to reach base camp.

Sources indicate that the team has completed two acclimatization climbs, looking for a passage through the icefall at the base of the mountain and then a series of couloirs. They reached 5,900m and, on a second trip, 6,600m. Deep snow covered the peak, which slowed progress. Finally, they launched a summit bid last week.

From 6,600m, they spent a day on technical ice sections of 70–80º. In poor visibility, they endured spindrift and were showered by small ice chunks.

“In the afternoon, the weather deteriorated sharply,” Natalia Zanina stated. “Heavy snowfall began, and we started being struck by large, continuous avalanches. At 6,800m (340m from the summit), we decided to turn back.”.

A note on names: according to 8000ers.com, Asapurna should be the correct name for this peak because — although it is closer to Gangapurna — Asapurna’s summit ridge connects directly to Annapurna III.

It has been revealed that the list of climbing permits granted by Nepal’s Ministry of Tourism points to some other interesting expeditions, some of them in remote western Nepal. There is a permit for Nyalu Kang (6,265m), only opened to foreign climbers in 2024 and reportedly unclimbed, and Ardang, summited once by Canadians Bryce Kendall and Sunny Twelker in 2019. Victor Saunders and Mick Fowler of the UK attempted Ardang last year.

Industry News: Won the Lottery? Stay Quiet and Hire a Team Before You Claim

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that before you claim a big lottery prize, lock up the ticket, tell almost no one, and hire a tax attorney, a CPA, and a fee-only financial planner, one paid only by you.
  • In a recent development, that 24% is only the IRS withholding rate on a prize over $5,000.
  • In a recent development, put the ticket in a safe deposit box, and tell no one but your spouse or partner until your team is hired.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that before you claim a big lottery prize, lock up the ticket, tell almost no one, and hire a tax attorney, a CPA, and a fee-only financial planner, one paid only by you. Choose the lump sum or annuity with them, and expect to owe more federal tax than the 24% withheld.

In a recent development, that 24% is only the IRS withholding rate on a prize over $5,000. A jackpot is taxed almost entirely at the top 37% rate, so roughly another 13 cents of every dollar comes due at tax time.

In a recent development, put the ticket in a safe deposit box, and tell no one but your spouse or partner until your team is hired. Ask the attorney before you sign the back, since the lottery pays whoever’s name is written there.

In a recent development, in Ohio, a trust can claim the prize, and the lottery’s announcement names the trust instead of you. Powerball tickets typically expire 90 days to a year after the drawing, depending on the state, so check your state’s deadline and whether it lets winners stay anonymous.

Industry observers note that then comes the payout. Mega Millions and Powerball pay the annuity in 30 installments over 29 years, each 5% bigger than the last. The lump sum is the cash it takes to fund them, such as $450.5 million for a $1.04 billion Powerball jackpot won in August 2026.

It has been revealed that taking the annuity saves little federal tax, since even Mega Millions’ $50 million starting jackpot pays about $752,000 the first year, past where the top rate starts for a single filer. State tax depends on where you bought the ticket and where you live, and California doesn’t tax its own lottery’s prizes. So choose the payout by how you handle money. The annuity keeps you from spending it all early, and the lump sum suits you only if you’ll invest it and leave it alone.

While you plan, park the money and wait before any big purchase. Then pay off high-interest debt, fill an emergency reserve, fund retirement accounts, and set a yearly gift budget before the requests start. Keep working until the plan is written down.

Even a prize of a few thousand dollars is taxable income, and no federal tax is withheld at $5,000 or less, so set aside your tax bracket’s percentage of it the day you cash it.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as we pointed out last week, most victims of animal attacks around the world are not tourists but the people who live amid potentially dangerous animals all the time.
  • It has been revealed that chamois in France.
  • A normally timid mountain ungulate has been attacking runners on the outskirts of Besançon in eastern France.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as we pointed out last week, most victims of animal attacks around the world are not tourists but the people who live amid potentially dangerous animals all the time. Here are some incidents that have come to light recently.

It has been revealed that chamois in France. Photo: Ludovic Laude/L’Est Republicain.

A normally timid mountain ungulate has been attacking runners on the outskirts of Besançon in eastern France.

One victim, a 30-year-old woman jogger, was knocked unconscious and suffered a punctured shoulder and serious scalp wounds requiring stitches and staples. The incident occurred just a few hundred meters from the outskirts of the city.

It has been revealed that “I didn’t hear it coming,” the woman, known only as Milena, told Le Monde. “I only had time to see its head 10 centimeters from me, and then, nothing, total blackout…”.

The woman was unconscious for about five minutes.

Recent findings suggest that another runner had been attacked days earlier. The incidents occurred near La Chapelle des Buis. Wildlife authorities described the behavior as highly unusual and authorized the animal’s removal. The cause of its aggression remains unclear.

A 71-year-old Winter Garden, Florida fisherman, Steven Hamilton, was posing for a photograph with a fish when a large alligator lunged from the water, seized his leg, and pulled him into a pond.

Emergency crews responded, but the alligator refused to let go of his body, according to Fox News. By the time they released him and killed the alligator, Hamilton was dead. The medical examiner identified drowning and blunt-force injury to his left leg as causes of death, with alligator tooth marks on both sides of the leg.

Alligator attacks are rare but occur occasionally. According to the Florida Fish & Wildlife Conservation Commission, there have been a total of 500 alligator bites against humans since 1948, including 32 fatal encounters.

Industry observers note that asiatic black bear. Photo: Shutterstock.

Vladimir Odulo, a fisherman from Primorye in Russia’s Far East, survived an attack by an Asiatic black bear, also known as a Himalayan bear.

The bear attacked while Odulo was fishing. He tried to defend himself with his fishing rod, but the animal knocked him into the water. Odulo continued fighting as it “beat his face like a boxer,” Russian media reported the fisherman saying. Suddenly, the bear stopped the attack and fled into the forest.

Odulo suffered several wounds and a serious eye injury, but survived. Doctors in Vladivostok were able to save his eyesight.

In a recent development, A venomous Caspian cobra, which now occurs high in Himachal Pradesh. Photo: Shutterstock.

Two deaths in the Indian Himalaya have been attributed to Caspian cobras. Native to Central Asia, this venomous species has expanded its range eastward into the higher reaches of Himachal Pradesh. It now also occurs in Pakistan and Kashmir.

The first death occurred when a 40-year-old man accidentally stepped on a Caspian cobra while spraying an apple orchard. Wearing open-toed footwear, he sustained two bites on his leg. He was taken to a local faith healer before being shifted to the hospital, where he was declared dead, according to the Tribune of India.

In the second case, a 62-year-old man stepped on a snake while on his way to work and was bitten on the leg. He collapsed within half an hour and was taken to a health facility, where he died.

These fatalities occurred some time ago, but the report on them was published just this week in the journal Epidemiology International. The Caspian cobra generally inhabits higher, open, rocky terrain at elevations of 2,000m or higher, where both incidents occurred. Researchers suggest its range may now include lower elevations.

Industry observers note that A charging elephant. Photo: Shutterstock.

Two men died in separate elephant attacks in northern Kenya.

Industry observers note that on October 11, Eisimgai Gorow Ltarakwa, 41, was herding goats near Nguposorogin village when a lone elephant attacked him. He suffered severe injuries and died at the scene.

Two days later, Mukhtar Abdoy Hussein, 64, was grazing livestock near Benane village when a herd of elephants trampled him to death.

The incident highlights the risks faced by herders in areas where livestock grazing activities bring communities into close proximity with wildlife. Under a conservation initiative, the families are entitled to receive compensation, according to Kenyan media.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, start your holiday budget from a total you can pay off by January, then split it into a line for every cost of the season, not just gifts. Give each person on your gift list an amount, and log every purchase under its line so you spot overspending in time to cut back.

The National Retail Federation expects holiday retail sales of $1.013 trillion this November and December, up 4.2% from $972 billion in 2025. In its 2025 holiday survey, consumers planned to spend $890.49 each on average, and $262.56 of that was for seasonal items such as food, candy, decorations, and cards rather than gifts.

A budget that lists only gifts misses that spending, along with costs like the flight home, year-end tips for a sitter or house cleaner, and a party outfit. Give each of those costs its own budget line, all under one total, set at what you can pay off by January.

Set up these lines, each with a dollar amount:.

Your card and bank statements from last November and December show what you spent on each of these, so start every line except gifts at last year’s amount. Say you can pay off $1,200, and the lines other than gifts add up to $700. That leaves $500 for gifts, or $50 each for 10 people on your list. If $50 a person is too little, draw names in your family, buy only for the kids, or give joint or homemade gifts.

Industry observers note that move money into a separate savings account with each paycheck, and pay for the holidays from it, so no holiday purchase ends up as credit card debt. Log each purchase under its line the day you make it, in a spreadsheet or a budgeting app.

Cover a shortfall on one line by moving money from another line, never by raising the total.

Track each line from your phone with one of the best budgeting apps.

Breaking: A 76-Year-Old Kazakh Blacksmith Is Walking Around the World

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that sarsenbay Kotyrashov had never left his native Kazakhstan when, in 2023, he set out to walk across the Caucasus.
  • Industry observers note that now, three years later, Kotyrashov has almost 30,000 followers on Instagram who have tuned in for his journeys on foot across Eurasia.
  • Alongside his growing social media presence, Kotyrashov has been working with UNESCO to document Kazakh artisanal practices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sarsenbay Kotyrashov had never left his native Kazakhstan when, in 2023, he set out to walk across the Caucasus. A blacksmith from the industrial province of Ulytau in central Kazakhstan, Kotyrashov had in tow only a battered suitcase and his signature leather hat as he crossed the Kazakh border. He was 73 years old.

Industry observers note that now, three years later, Kotyrashov has almost 30,000 followers on Instagram who have tuned in for his journeys on foot across Eurasia. People stop him and ask for selfies with Ulytauman, his online moniker and a reference to his home province.

Alongside his growing social media presence, Kotyrashov has been working with UNESCO to document Kazakh artisanal practices. He is now 76, and his travels are far from over.

It has been revealed that kotyrashov started his first job at age nine, working as a herder. By the time he entered his 70s, he had worked an astonishing diversity of manual labor jobs: carpenter, joiner, stonemason, lathe operator, metalworker, and most recently blacksmith. His expertise in traditional artisanship landed him a job at the Ulytau National Reserve Museum, a 150,000-hectare open-air museum comprising everything from mountains to mausoleums. From 2010 to 2020, Kotyrashov worked restoring historical buildings on the reserve, some of which date back to the Bronze Age.

Sources indicate that the mausoleum of Jochi Khan, a 12th century Mongol ruler, is only one of the 25 building complexes at the Ulytau National Museum Reserve. Photo: Wikimedia Commons.

Tourists came from around the world to visit the reserve. Kotyrashov began to dream of traveling like them. “Why not?” he asked himself. “Why haven’t I seen the whole world myself? In my entire life, I’ve only ever seen Ulytau and Astana.”.

Industry observers note that then came the pandemic, and his wife of 40 years passed away. Kotyrashov built a small hand-cart and set out across Kazakhstan on foot. “I chose to travel on foot, because when you walk, you notice much more, including nature, landscapes, animals, and plants,” he explained. “There is also time to think, to reflect, and to understand things.”.

Kotyrashov’s first journey in 2022 was a love letter to Kazakhstan. As he walked from town to town over 181 days, pulling a homemade cart weighing around 60kg, he spoke with local artisans about their crafts. He tied a flag to his cart to promote the Qymyzmuryndyk festival, which celebrates the traditional Kazakh drink of kumis, or fermented mare’s milk. Local governments began holding press conferences for him and organizing lodging.

Photo: Sarsenbay Kotyrashov/Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that “Each day, I would meet with anywhere from 150 to 500 people in different parts of the country,” he told a Kazakh outlet. “The greatest discovery of my journey was the people — the citizens of Kazakhstan. They are generous, kind, noble, and open-hearted; I was truly struck by the kind of people who inhabit our Kazakhstan. It gives me hope for a better future.”.

It has been revealed that in 2023, he crossed the border into Russia, then followed the spine of the Caucasus Mountains through Chechnya and Georgia, and finally into Türkiye. Sometimes, he bivouacked in his sleeping bag. In towns, though, Chechen and Ingush Georgian locals invited him to stay with them. In Türkiye, he slept in mosques.

In a recent development, kotyrashov decorated his cart with flags celebrating Kazakhstan. Photo: Kazinform.

After his trip to Türkiye, Kotyrashov tackled China. Unlike in Central Asia and the Caucasus, he finally had to pay for hotels. By now, though, he had secured a trip coordinator and sponsors who helped him cover the costs. He took photos at the Great Wall and ended his journey in Beijing.

Sources indicate that europe posed greater difficulties. Everywhere else he had visited, he walked along the side of the highway. Unbeknownst to him when he began his 2026 trip, 3,000km from Belgrade to Paris, walking on highways is largely illegal in Europe. He had replaced his cart with an old suitcase, but the suitcase bit the dust on an unpaved footpath 150km outside Paris.

In a recent development, but Kotyrashov had an appointment. Determined to make it, he left the suitcase behind and sped on with his backpack.

On April 24th, he arrived at the UNESCO World Heritage Center in Paris and presented officials there with a handmade iron bell. At the Center, he met with Kazakhstan’s permanent UNESCO representative and shared his research on Kazakh artisanship and nomadic travel.

Kotyrashov on the Great Wall of China. Photo: Astana Times.

After returning from Paris, Kotyrashov began working once more as a blacksmith to save up for his next trip. Sponsors help him with lodging and food, but he still needs to pay for his own gear. “Over the course of six months, I wore out seven pairs of shoes,” he noted.

Recent findings suggest that in 2027, he will set out to another continent: the Americas. He aims to cross the United States from coast to coast, starting in Florida and ending in California. After his experience in Europe, he’s studying up on American highway law.

Industry observers note that three years ago, Kotyrashov left Kazakhstan for the first time. Now, he’s hoping the American trip will contribute to his broader goal of claiming a Guinness record for the most miles walked by a person over 75.

According to recent reports, “I had never traveled far in my life,” he stated. “But it is never too late to travel.”.

Photo: Sarsenbay Kotyrashov/Instagram.

Year          Route                                                                                   Distance.

2022      Across Kazakhstan, ending in Aktau on the Caspian Sea       ~8,000km.

2023     Atyrau, Kazakhstan → Russia → Caucasus → Türkiye             ~3,000km.

2024     Kazakhstan → Russian Altai → Mongolia → China                   uncertain.

2026    Belgrade → Hungary → Austria → Germany → Paris                 ~3,000km.

Amelia Earhart Search Find Trees, Not Plane. Mystery Remains

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.
  • A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.
  • Their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.

A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.

Their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos. While some hoped the anomaly was the remnants of Earhart’s Lockheed Electra, the expedition determined it was entirely natural.

Recent findings suggest that the Taraia Object on a satellite image. Located at Nikumaroro. Photo: Archaeological Legacy Institute.

According to Purdue University officials, the object was a cluster of large fallen trees resting on a sandbar. Much of the debris observed in satellite images had already broken up and washed away, leaving a single Y-shaped piece. The reflective, metallic glint seen from above turned out to be a hardened layer of coral sand coating the wood.

On the way to the atoll. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

The five-day operation proved logistically complicated. Workers faced dense brush and a large population of giant coconut crabs. The nocturnal activities of the massive crabs forced the crew to abandon plans to camp on the atoll and to return to the ship each evening. During the day, the crabs simply minded their own business.

One of the crew holds a coconut crab. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Despite the difficulties, researchers recovered a few minor artifacts to study lagoon drift patterns, including a 76cm steel tube.

The team emphasized that ruling out the Taraia Object does not disprove the broader “castaway hypothesis.” For decades, historians have investigated the theory that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan drifted off course during their 1937 global circumnavigation attempt, landing on Nikumaroro’s reef after failing to find Howland Island.

Industry observers note that amelia Earhart. Photo: amelia.prf.org.

Purdue University, where Earhart once served as a career counselor and aviation advisor, stated that its commitment to the search remains unchanged.

“Amelia Earhart never gave up — she kept pushing boundaries and flying into the unknown,” said Steve Schultz, Purdue’s general counsel and field assistant, after the expedition. “She kept flying, and we will keep searching.”.

For more details, extensive project documentation, and a gallery of expedition photographs, you can visit the official mission site at Amelia.prf.org.

From left to right: Steve Schultz, Sirisha Bandla, and Marc Hagle, members of the research team. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Jost Kobusch Will Try Again to Solo Winter Everest

📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project.
  • Industry observers note that “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb.
  • Kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project. His long-term goal is to climb solo in winter, without oxygen, self-supported, and via the Lho La and the West Ridge.

Industry observers note that “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb. In this case, his strategy is to arrive at the mountain in the best shape possible, physically and mentally.

Kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon. The group soon moved to Manang in the Annapurna region and began acclimatizing in the Chulu range.

According to recent reports, jost Kobusch (in yellow) scouts around Manang. Photo: Alex Pichon.

It has been revealed that the proposal was to spend a few nights at altitude and traverse the four Chulu peaks, all above 6,000m. “[However,] expeditions rarely unfold exactly as expected,” Kobusch admitted.

A member in the team felt exhausted after reaching the summit of the second peak, and the group abandoned the traverse there. “At least, we traversed from the summit of Chulu Far East (6,059m) to the top of Chulu East (6,444m) from the southeast,” Kobusch mentioned. He indicates their line between the two peaks was upcoming.

The line followed by Kobusch and his team up Chulu East. Photo: Alex Pichon.

Their next blueprint will be to climb a 7,000m peak in the area before Kobusch moves to the Khumbu in November. “I want to reach 8,000m, but on a different mountain than Everest, before the beginning of winter,” he said.

Industry observers note that he wants to be completely acclimatized by the time he starts working on Everest on December 22, the start of calendar winter. Kobusch will have two photographers in Base Camp, but he will climb alone.

Acclimatization in Manang, Photo: Alex Pichon.

Industry observers note that “I need to be able to move efficiently, make good decisions when I’m tired, manage risk alone, and stay comfortable in an environment where very small mistakes can have very serious consequences,” Kobusch recently wrote on social media. He says that so far, all is going well. “I’m feeling good, I’ve done my homework, and I will start again on Everest better prepared than ever.”.

Kobusch has attempted winter Everest solo on three previous occasions, always via the Lho La and the West Ridge, thus avoiding venturing alone into the Khumbu Icefall.

In his first attempt in 2019-20, he reached the West Shoulder and pushed above 7,300m. On the second attempt in 2021-22, high winds didn’t let him go beyond 6,400m. He planned to try again the following year, but he caught dengue fever while training in Nepal and had to cancel.

Once recovered, he soloed Denali in February-March 2023. Everest had to wait one more year, this time due to a back injury. On the third attempt in 2024-25, he reached his highest point yet: 7,537m on December 27.

Kobusch’s highest point is shown with a green circle, and the Hornbein Couloir is the pink line on the 3D map by RealityMaps.

“The chances of success are not particularly high,” he recently wrote. “If I had to put a number on it, I would say around 20%. But that does not make the attempt meaningless. If anything, it is part of what makes it interesting.”.

Air France-KLM Flying Blue → Tahiti Business Class

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2552 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The only points path to nonstop business class service to French Polynesia.
  • Sources indicate that picture this: you're reclining in a fully flat bed somewhere over the Pacific, a glass of Champagne in hand, watching the sun melt into the ocean from 35,000 feet.
  • The core insight here is deceptively simple: Air France-KLM's Flying Blue program is the only way to book the only nonstop flight between Los Angeles and Tahiti using points — and that program happens to offer some of the most generous award pricing in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The only points path to nonstop business class service to French Polynesia.

Sources indicate that picture this: you're reclining in a fully flat bed somewhere over the Pacific, a glass of Champagne in hand, watching the sun melt into the ocean from 35,000 feet. In eight hours, you'll land in Papeete — French Polynesia's gateway to overwater bungalows, turquoise lagoons, and the kind of trip people save their whole lives for. And you got here on points. This is the Air France business class seat to Tahiti, and it represents one of the most emotionally resonant redemptions in the entire travel rewards ecosystem. Not just because of where you're going — though Tahiti is bucket-list by definition — but because of the staggering gap between what you'd pay in cash and what you'll pay in miles. **The math will genuinely stop you in your tracks.** A business class ticket from Los Angeles (LAX) to Papeete (PPT) on Air France regularly retails between **$5,000 and $12,000 per person**. That's the cash reality. But with Flying Blue miles — Air France-KLM's frequent flyer program — you can book the same seat for as few as **88,000 miles**. At the high end of retail pricing, that's a value of **13.6 cents per point (CPP)**. Even at the low end, you're extracting **5.7 CPP** from miles that most programs value at 1–2 cents. In the ChooseFI community, we talk constantly about optimizing every dollar toward financial independence — and a redemption that turns 88,000 transferable points into a $5,000–$12,000 experience is about as powerful as it gets. Here's what makes this feel different from your average business class booking: Air France operates a **Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner** on this route, featuring a modern, premium business class cabin with direct aisle access for every seat, noise-reducing windows, better humidity levels, and that unmistakably French touch in service and catering. You're not just flying in a recliner — you're flying in a genuine lie-flat pod on one of aviation's most celebrated aircraft. And this is the only nonstop option. Air France is the **sole carrier operating nonstop LAX–PPT** service. That's not a coincidence — it's a pricing inefficiency baked into the route's geography, and it's exactly the kind of structural advantage the ChooseFI community knows how to exploit.

The core insight here is deceptively simple: Air France-KLM's Flying Blue program is the only way to book the only nonstop flight between Los Angeles and Tahiti using points — and that program happens to offer some of the most generous award pricing in the world.

Flying Blue uses a dynamic award pricing model, meaning costs fluctuate based on demand and availability. That sounds like a disadvantage — and sometimes it is. But here's the inefficiency: Flying Blue releases Promo Rewards every single month. These are fixed-price award seats on select routes, discounted 25–50% off standard award pricing. When Tahiti appears as a Promo Reward destination (which it does periodically), the pricing drops dramatically — and crucially, Promo Reward tickets eliminate carrier-imposed fuel surcharges entirely.

Sources indicate that fuel surcharges on Air France-operated flights are normally moderate, but they're real — they can add $200–$500 to an award ticket. Promo Rewards wipe those out. This is the pricing inefficiency: Flying Blue is essentially subsidizing this cabin to drive demand, and you can capture the subsidy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that you can decorate a rental your way without losing the deposit if every change either comes off clean or swaps back to the original at move-out.
  • Bare walls, a glaring ceiling light, and dated cabinet knobs don’t have to last as long as the lease.
  • Each of the 40 ideas below passes the same move-out test.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that you can decorate a rental your way without losing the deposit if every change either comes off clean or swaps back to the original at move-out. Choose peel-off, plug-in, and freestanding pieces, bag every knob or fixture you replace, and get the landlord’s written okay before you paint, drill, or touch the plumbing.

Bare walls, a glaring ceiling light, and dated cabinet knobs don’t have to last as long as the lease.

Each of the 40 ideas below passes the same move-out test. A rug, a lamp, or a tension rod comes off without a trace. A cabinet knob or a showerhead swaps back, because the original waits out the lease in a labeled bag.

It has been revealed that take a small kitchen with one 8-by-9-foot wall by the table and 20 cabinet knobs. Three rolls of peel-and-stick wallpaper at $25 each cover the wall, a $35 runner goes in front of the sink, and two $20 ten-packs replace the knobs, which go in a bag in a drawer. That’s $150. At move-out the paper peels off, the runner rolls up, and the old knobs go back on, so the landlord has nothing to take out of a $1,500 security deposit. Flat or freshly painted walls can lift with the paper, so test a small piece inside a closet for a week before you cover the wall.

Photograph every wall, floor, and fixture before you change it, since those pictures are your proof of the rental’s condition when you ask for your security deposit back.

Give every adhesive below the same closet test, from picture strips to backsplash tile, and remove each one slowly at move-out.

The Consumer Product Safety Commission’s Anchor It! campaign reminds renters as well as owners to anchor furniture to the wall, and it notes that patching the hole afterward takes minutes. Each anchor takes a screw, so get the landlord’s written okay before you put one in.

Put every original you swap out, from cabinet knobs to the showerhead, in bags labeled by room and taped inside a kitchen cabinet, so nothing is missing on move-out day.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hidesuke Taneishi and Tetsu Hashimoto of Japan are missing on unclimbed Gangapurna West in Nepal’s Annapurna region.
  • The Japanese pair headed to the 7,140m peak in September, and we heard no further news of them.
  • Hidesuke Taneishi, left, and Tetsu Hashimoto, right, with a support team member in Kathmandu earlier this week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hidesuke Taneishi and Tetsu Hashimoto of Japan are missing on unclimbed Gangapurna West in Nepal’s Annapurna region.

The Japanese pair headed to the 7,140m peak in September, and we heard no further news of them. After a major storm hit Nepal’s mountains three weeks ago, we presumed they had retreated. But now it seems they did not. They have been out of touch since October 15, after encountering severe weather conditions during their attempt to climb the peak, According to News on Nepal.

Hidesuke Taneishi, left, and Tetsu Hashimoto, right, with a support team member in Kathmandu earlier this week. Photo: Cosmo Adventure.

The Russian team that reached the mountain earlier this month reportedly found no sign of the Japanese climbers on the peak. Bad weather forced the Russians down from their summit attempt at 6,800m.

A helicopter search-and-rescue operation is now underway, Manang Chief District Officer Mukti Prasad Khanal has confirmed. Today, high-altitude helicopters and drones successfully recovered some of their gear, including trekking poles, near 7,050m, but the climbers themselves remain missing.

Gangapurna West is also known as Asapurna or Peak Lachenal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that some big employers still give part-time workers health insurance. Most require about 20 hours a week, and a few set no hours minimum. Before you apply, find out how many hours you’ll need, how long you’ll wait, and whether the plan covers hospital care or pays only set dollar amounts.

Employers like these are the exception. In March 2026, just 23% of part-time workers in private industry had access to medical benefits through work, against 87% of those working full time, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Under the Affordable Care Act, an employer with at least 50 full-time workers, counting part-timers’ hours toward that total, can owe the IRS a payment if it doesn’t offer coverage to employees who average 30 hours a week. A part-timer who gets a tax credit for a Marketplace strategy, the health coverage people buy on their own, can’t trigger that payment, so covering part-timers is each employer’s choice.

It has been revealed that each employer also sets its own hours requirement. Nine of the 10 below publish theirs, from none to 20 hours a week, and at REI and U-Haul some part-timers get a more limited plan than full-timers do.

The Marketplace at HealthCare.gov sells individual health intends, and income-based tax credits can lower the premium.

Industry observers note that A job’s offer that you turn down keeps you from those credits only if it’s affordable and meets the minimum value standard. That standard asks for a proposal built to pay at least 60% of medical costs, with substantial coverage for hospital stays and doctor visits.

Most job prepares meet it, so ask the employer whether its part-time strategy does before you enroll.

The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The three-man Russian team returned to Everest’s West Ridge but found the route even more difficult than they expected. After two days of struggle, they’re heading back to Base Camp.

Recent findings suggest that on October 20, Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov went back up to the Lho La and pitched their tent on the wide plateau beyond. They still had time to fix more rope higher up.

“We moved…over terrain we’d already covered on the previous rotation,” the climbers texted to team member Natalya Belyankina, who had to abandon the expedition due to illness.

It has been revealed that “The weather is good: sunny, with light winds, but cold,” they noted. “Progress was painfully slow today due to heavy packs and a persistent cough,” the climbers noted later.

In a recent development, on Wednesday, they hoped to reach 7,500m, spend the night there, check the route ahead, and then retreat to the plateau. However, they didn’t get as far as they had planned.

“We didn’t cover much ground today,” leader Andrei Vsiliev texted Anna Piunova of The Mountain Club. “The route is no walk in the park. We have to climb steep snowy slopes that conceal rock sections underneath.”.

According to recent reports, to make things worse, they found no suitable bivy spots at their highest point, so they had to retreat to a place where they could pitch their tent for the night. Today, they were just too exhausted to keep going.

Sources indicate that “We’re heading down; we’re sick and need to recover,” Vasiliev told Belyankina. “We can barely keep moving.”.

#9420. Breaking: Six Dumb Misconceptions About The Economy (that the Politicians Want You To Believe)

📅 13 Oct 2024 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1999 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mrmoneymustache ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Six Dumb Misconceptions About The Economy (that the Politicians Want You To Believe)

📅 13 Oct 2024 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1999 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Well, it looks like we’re here in another US election year already.
  • As Advanced Mustachians, we already know that the ongoing battle of Harris vs.
  • It has been revealed that but out of all the things the politicians like to bicker about, there’s one area where MMM does need to set the record straight, and that area is of course money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Well, it looks like we’re here in another US election year already.

As Advanced Mustachians, we already know that the ongoing battle of Harris vs. Trump should not be consuming much of our time. Sure, we do our research and cast our votes but after that we move right on to focus on other things within our own circle of control.

It has been revealed that but out of all the things the politicians like to bicker about, there’s one area where MMM does need to set the record straight, and that area is of course money. Your money, the economy in general, and the overall wealth of the nation.

Politicians are already not known for being the sharpest tools in the shed when it comes to technical stuff like science, technology, or economics. But this year the discourse has become particularly dumb, as our candidates try to manipulate undecided voters in swing states with ideas that are based on irrational emotions rather than sound economic sense.

For one particularly funny example, you may have noticed that the competing party (Trump in this case) is attacking the incumbents (Biden/Harris) over the “bad economy.” When in fact the US economy is stronger than it has ever been, with the lowest unemployment we’ve ever seen as well.

It’s hard to imagine a better situation than we have right now, and in fact the recent bout of higher inflation is a sign that things have been going too well, and we needed to step on the brakes with the help of higher interest rates.

But somehow the people still seem to believe that we have a “bad” economy. Take a look at this Gallup poll showing that while most people (85%) are doing really well right now, they assume that it’s just their own good fortune – only 17% believe the economy is doing well.

This is mathematically impossible, because if most people are doing well, that’s the definition of a good economy! And suspiciously enough, this widespread wrongness correlates quite nicely with the rise of social media misinformation.

So the politicians and the news have been doing the opposite of what they should be doing in an ideal situation (sharing accurate information). And sure, we can always just ignore their speeches and go on with our lives. But when it comes to economics, knowledge is power (and money). The more accurately we understand how things really work, the wealthier we will all become.

So with all that in mind, I hereby present you with my list of the….

Top Dumb Things Politicians Want You To Believe About The Economy.

1: The President Controls the Economy.

If there’s a recession, the opposition party likes to blame it on the current president. If the economy is booming, the current president likes to give himself (or possibly soon herself) credit for all of that success. But really, the US economy is way too substantial – and thankfully way too free – for the president to control or really even influence all that strongly.

In a recent development, in reality, our economy is a gigantic machine which converts labor and materials into things like iPhones, hospitals and pumpkin pies. And although we’re the biggest economy at 26% of the planet, we are still heavily influenced by that much bigger 74% of economic activity that the other 7.6 billion people on Earth are busy producing everywhere else.

When we have our inevitable little boom and bust cycles, they are mostly caused by the normal cycle of irrational exuberance (and greed) like the 2007 housing boom, followed by brief periods of extreme fear and pessimism like the 2008-2012 financial and housing crash.

It has been revealed that the government does play a role too, by setting tax rates and other rules. But the effects of these policies are usually so delayed and unpredictable, that you can’t draw a straight line between today’s president and today’s economy. In other words, the government does its best to adjust the rudder on our giant ship, but in the short term our economy lurches around on the waves and storms of the ocean.

2: The President Controls Interest Rates.

Recent findings suggest that this one is especially funny to me, as our candidates feign sympathy for the hard life of middle class Americans, who now face higher borrowing costs on their credit cards and car loans and mortgages. They claim they will fight to bring the interest rates down. Trump even goes as far as bullying our Federal Reserve board members (who can only do their jobs if we allow them to function as independent experts) and suggesting that he would take over the whole department, if elected.

The real story is that while monetary policy would be a terrible tool to leave in the hands of a sitting president (see Argentina), it does function as an excellent set of gas and brake pedals for the economy if used properly. When things slow down and unemployment gets too high, a cut to the interest rates will produce a boost in everything from new jobs to stock prices. But if things get too hot, you get rapid inflation which can mess up the system.

3: Inflation has Made Life Harder for Americans (and the President Can Magically Reverse it).

Sources indicate that this line of reasoning is even dumber than the last one. For a couple of years after the Covid era, we had rapid inflation. It was caused by a rare combination of a goods shortage caused by things like factory closures and remote work, plentiful demand from government stimulus spending and low interest rates. These factors have since ironed themselves out, and inflation is back down to an ultra-low 2.4%.

But most significantly, wages have still risen faster than inflation so we are all better off than before! Since 2019, overall prices are up 19% and our wages are up 21%. So even after all that inflation, we are still doing just fine. But the candidates are still bickering over inflation as if it’s an actual problem, and even worse promising to “bring prices back down”. And they’ve managed to convince the electorate that “higher wages and prices” is the same thing as “a bad economy”. Which is just plain wrong.

In a recent development, bonus dumbness: politicians also occasionally blame “greedy corporations” for increasing prices to hoard profits. While price increases are totally acceptable in a market system (as a business owner you are free to set prices wherever you like), in reality it doesn’t usually happen because our markets are too competitive. For example, a recent deep analysis from NPR indicated that no, grocery stores haven’t made any windfall profit at all off of this recent bout of Covid-fueled inflation.

4: The President Controls Housing Prices.

Sources indicate that one important thing that has changed over the past ten years is that US house prices and rents have both risen much faster than general inflation and even wages. On the positive side, interest rates have also risen which tends to make houses feel more expensive and is supposed to help bring house prices down. But it hasn’t happened yet which means we have the double whammy of higher prices and higher interest costs for mortgage borrowers.

The dumb part is that our candidates are proposing things that would make the problem even worse, like subsidies for first-time homebuyers or schemes to reduce the interest rates. When really the solution is to increase the supply of housing, which I personally think will happen if we stop putting up roadblocks for homebuilders (myself included) to build housing.

Things like faster and cheaper permits, less onerous and expensive building codes, eliminating suburban-style zoning and setback and car parking rules, and changing laws so that NIMBYs no longer get any say over what other people do with their own land could all help reduce the cost of building a house by about 50%, quickly and permanently.

5: The President Controls Gas Prices, and They Are At the moment “High” and We Want Them Lower.

Sources indicate that ahh, gasoline! The most ridiculous of things to worry about and the fuel for many of MMM’s rants since 2011.

First of all, on an inflation-adjusted basis, gasoline is still about the same price as it was in 1950: in the $3-4 range per gallon, in today’s dollars.

Secondly, it is so cheap that even with our huge inefficient American vehicles, the average household is still only spending 2.5% of their disposable income on the stuff! (The funny part is that they spend many times more on the rest of the car ownership experience while thinking gas is the part that is expensive).

It has been revealed that third, gasoline has been obsolete for almost a decade now. You can get a used electric car for less than the price of a comparable used gas car, or if you’re a fancypants money waster like me, new EVs are also cheaper than their gas counterparts. You get a faster, nicer car that almost never needs maintenance OR gasoline, and save money.

So why are we even still talking about this antique fuel of a previous era? Why aren’t the candidates also arguing over the price of Kodak film or typewriters or fax machines?

6: The Economy is Something We Should Even Worry About.

It has been revealed that the funniest part about all this economic talk is that we’re focusing on the wrong thing. While hard work and business and advancing the frontiers of human knowledge are all fun things, the reality is that we passed the point of having “Enough” decades ago. When the American middle class complains about how hard we have it these days, it’s like a bunch of overfed people at a buffet wishing they could just have one more flavor of donuts stacked onto the table.

Yes, we have income and wealth inequality so that the rich tend to get richer more quickly. And yes, we should keep that in check with a somewhat progressive tax system because a more equal society tends to be a more peaceful and happy one.

Sources indicate that but have you noticed that as the rich people get richer, they don’t get any happier? It’s because after you pass the point of “Enough”, adding more money doesn’t really help much.

According to recent reports, and “Enough” is much more defined by your mindset (and your collection of life skills) than your paycheck. So if the politicians really cared about improving our happiness and wellbeing, they’d be preaching the Principles of Mustachianism rather than pandering to the specific requests of coal miners or billionaires.

It has been revealed that but alas, winning an election is a very different thing than proposing stuff that is actually best for the country. And for that reason, we cast our votes for the best party and then tune back out until the next election.

In the Comments: Has the election season been getting you down, pumping you up, or just giving you a thorough dose of “Meh”?

Sources indicate that while researching economic stats for this article, I came across a quirky but informative series of videos called USA Facts by none other than former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer. It seems that he had the same frustration as me: Americans are fighting over a bunch of opinions and misinformation without even bothering to look up the actual facts. So he made a well-produced series of videos that just share the facts without the baggage of political hype on top of them. I wish our politicians could do the same thing!

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Grocery Delivery Costs More Than the Delivery Fee – Check the Pickup Price First

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A grocery delivery order can carry a service fee, a tip, and marked-up prices besides its delivery fee.
  • Recent findings suggest that say a cart costs $100 in the store and $110 on a delivery app, where the store marks its prices up 10%.
  • It has been revealed that the $3.99 delivery fee is the smallest of those four charges, since the markups add $10, the service fee $5.50, and the tip $10.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A grocery delivery order can carry a service fee, a tip, and marked-up prices besides its delivery fee. Before you pay for delivery, price the same cart for curbside pickup in your store’s app, and buy a delivery membership only if you’d order often enough for it to save more than it costs.

Recent findings suggest that say a cart costs $100 in the store and $110 on a delivery app, where the store marks its prices up 10%. With a $3.99 delivery fee, a 5% service fee, and a $10 tip, the app order comes to about $129 before tax.

It has been revealed that the $3.99 delivery fee is the smallest of those four charges, since the markups add $10, the service fee $5.50, and the tip $10. On Instacart, each store sets its own prices, and some stores add a markup to help pay for delivery. The service fee varies with the store and the size of the cart.

Each store’s page on Instacart states, under its logo, whether its prices match what it charges in the store. Check that line before you fill the cart.

Curbside pickup through your store’s own app has no delivery fee and no driver to tip. At Walmart, pickup is free on orders over $35, and delivering the same order costs up to $9.95 without a membership.

Delivery can still come out ahead. It saves the drive and the time in the store, and ordering from a list can cut impulse buys. Pay for it when that time is worth more to you than the extra charges. It makes the least sense on a small order, where the delivery fee takes a bigger share of the bill.

A membership pays off only for frequent orders. Divide its yearly price by the delivery fee it saves to find how many orders it takes to pay for itself. Walmart+ costs $98 a year and waives that fee on orders over $35, so at $9.95 a delivery, 10 orders cover it. Amazon Prime members already get free same-day grocery delivery in most areas on any order above $25.

Build your next cart in your store’s app, and check its pickup total against the delivery total before you pay.

#9411. 8 Types of Financial Advisors – Hire for Your Problem, Then Ask Who Pays Them

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1192 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

8 Types of Financial Advisors – Hire for Your Problem, Then Ask Who Pays Them

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1192 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A financial advisor can be a planner, a broker, an insurance agent, or a tax pro, each trained and paid differently.
  • The title on the business card won’t tell you which one you’re dealing with.
  • Industry observers note that the license, registration, and credential behind the title tell you what you’re getting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A financial advisor can be a planner, a broker, an insurance agent, or a tax pro, each trained and paid differently. Name your problem first, whether it’s taxes, an estate, investing, insurance, debt, or a whole initiative. Then hire the professional built for it, and find out how they’re paid, since their pay can affect what they recommend.

The title on the business card won’t tell you which one you’re dealing with. FINRA, which oversees brokers, calls “financial advisor” a generic job title, one that investment professionals without any specific credential or license sometimes use.

Industry observers note that the license, registration, and credential behind the title tell you what you’re getting. FINRA’s BrokerCheck and the SEC’s Investment Adviser Public Disclosure site are free, and they show whether a broker or an investment adviser is registered, the licenses they hold, and any disciplinary history.

Then find out who pays them. A commission pays a professional when you buy or sell, so it rewards a sale, while a fee you pay directly doesn’t depend on which product you choose.

A financial planner looks at your money as a whole, from saving for college and retirement to taxes, insurance, and your estate, and gives you a blueprint to follow. Look for the Certified Financial Planner, or CFP, mark, which takes coursework, a bachelor’s degree, an exam, and thousands of hours of experience. It also commits the planner to act as a fiduciary, in your best interest, whenever giving you financial advice, and CFP Board’s verification tool demonstrates who holds it.

A fee-only planner takes no commissions, while a fee-based one earns fees and commissions, so part of their pay can depend on what you buy. Hire one when a decision or change affects several parts of your money at once, such as a new baby, an inheritance, or the move from a paycheck to retirement income.

It has been revealed that an investment adviser manages your investments and advises you on them over time, usually for a yearly fee based on your account’s value. At 1% a year, a $500,000 account pays $5,000, and the fee rises as the balance does. Advisers generally must register with the SEC or their state and must act in your best interest, and the SEC’s site shows the registration and any disciplinary history. Hire one when you’d rather hand the investment decisions to someone who keeps advising you.

Recent findings suggest that A robo-advisor is an online service that builds and manages a portfolio for you from your answers to a questionnaire. Most are registered investment advisers too, and their fees are often lower than a human adviser’s, usually a yearly percentage of your balance or, at some services, a flat monthly fee. Compare robo-advisors on that fee plus the expenses of the funds they buy, since both come out of your balance. A robo-advisor is a simple way to start investing when you don’t need help with taxes, insurance, or a plan.

A broker places trades for you and recommends what to buy, sell, or hold, earning a commission, or a markup added to the price, on each trade. Brokers must act in your best interest when they make a recommendation, but that duty doesn’t extend to monitoring your account afterward. BrokerCheck lists a broker’s licenses, such as the Series 7, which qualifies a broker to sell all kinds of securities.

Use one when you’ll make your own decisions and trade only now and then. Some professionals are both broker and adviser, so ask which role they’re in for each recommendation.

For taxes, look for a certified public accountant, licensed by a state board of accountancy, or an enrolled agent, licensed by the IRS after a three-part exam. Either one, like an attorney, can represent you before the IRS in any matter, including an audit, and the IRS’s directory of preparers with credentials highlights who holds which.

It has been revealed that few bill by the hour. Most charge for the return, starting from a base fee that rises with its forms or complexity, and the IRS warns against any preparer whose fee is a percentage of your refund. Pay one when your return needs more than tax software can handle, such as a rental, a business, or an IRS letter you don’t understand.

Recent findings suggest that an estate planning attorney drafts the documents that say who gets your property and who decides for you if you can’t, such as a will, a trust, and powers of attorney. Attorneys are licensed by their state’s courts or bar, so check with your state bar before you hire one. Many charge a flat fee to write a will and an hourly rate for other work, so get the fee agreement in writing. Hire one when you have children under 18, own a home or a business, or have a blended family.

An insurance agent sells policies such as life, disability, home, and auto coverage, and the insurer pays the agent a commission on each sale. A captive agent sells for one company, while an independent agent can sell policies from many, so you can compare quotes in one place. Make sure the agent is licensed in your state, which you can check with your state insurance department.

Talk to one when you’re buying coverage you’ll keep for years, such as life insurance or disability insurance. Price the same coverage directly from insurers too, since a policy bought direct may cost less without an agent’s commission.

A nonprofit credit counselor reviews your income, bills, and debts and helps you build a plan to pay them. If a debt management plan fits, you make one monthly payment to the agency, which pays your creditors, who may accept less interest or drop some fees.

Sources indicate that counseling is often free or low cost, though a plan can carry fees, so get any one-time or monthly fee quoted in writing. Look for a counselor certified by an outside group, such as the National Foundation for Credit Counseling. Call one when credit card or medical bills have grown past what you can pay down on your own.

According to recent reports, ask every candidate which license, registration, or credential they hold. Look up the record of a broker or an investment adviser on BrokerCheck or the SEC’s site, and check a planner’s CFP mark with CFP Board.

Sources indicate that last, ask whether they or their firm earn anything when you buy what they recommend. A yes doesn’t rule them out, but get a second opinion from someone you pay directly before you buy.

The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

Everyone would like a 12% yield that comes with little to no risk. With MITT-B (MITT.PR.B), investors can get that 12% yield.

Unfortunately, the risk decided to come along.

MITT-B is a preferred share from TPG Mortgage Investment Trust (MITT). Shares are right now trading around $16.94 and offer a stripped yield of approximately 12.10%.

That's a massive yield for a preferred share. However, it does come with our highest risk rating. MITT-B carries a risk rating of 5 on our scale from 1 to 5. Of all the preferred shares we cover, only two companies have preferred shares carrying that rating. MITT is one of them.

Sources indicate that if ever there was a "bad" preferred share, this would be one of them. Itâs not the worst, but itâs like the third worst porta-potty on day three of a music festival.

Sources indicate that is it bad? Well, in a way, yes. However, we're giving MITT-B a buy rating.

According to recent reports, because there's a difference between a risky preferred share and a bad investment. At the right price, even some of the riskiest preferred shares can be worth a purchase.

At the end of the day, a preferred share isn't bad just because it carries significant risk. It's a bad investment when investors arenât getting compensated for the risk they are taking on.

Let's start with the valuation.

MITT-B was trading around $16.94 as of writing this article. Our current price targets, which we upgrade regularly, are:.

Shares are in our buy range by a material amount.

Does anything stand out to you?

Now, to be fair, that's not because we think MITT-B isnât ever worth purchasing. There just happen to be other preferred shares and baby bonds with a much better relative valuation in our view. Some of those alternatives are trading in our strong buy range.

Not all buy ratings are created equal.

As an example, the preferred shares from Annaly Capital Management (NLY) come with a risk rating of 1. However, in recent history, they have been allergic to our buy range. When one of the preferred shares from NLY drops into our buy range, weâre generally interested in purchasing shares. We recently covered NLY-F when it had a stripped yield of 9.3%. At the time of writing that article, shares were close to our buy range.

According to recent reports, we spend a lot of time on relative valuations. Just because one of the preferred shares we cover enters our buy range doesnât automatically mean we make a purchase. There may be other preferred shares that are more attractive. In this case, there definitely are several of them.

In a recent development, MITT-B has a fixed coupon rate of 8%. That's not an absurd coupon rate for the preferred shares we cover. It isn't even unusual.

According to recent reports, investors are getting such a high yield because of the price. At $16.94, investors are purchasing shares at a significant discount to the $25 call value. Even though the price is down so low, investors are still entitled to the same dividend amount. The current yield is around 11.81%. However, we are using the stripped yield of 12.10% because it accounts for dividend accrual.

Either way, thatâs a lot of income for a preferred share.

Look at the common equity to preferred liquidation ratio: 0.95.

Itâs even uglier if you use market cap instead of common equity.

In a recent development, we like to see a substantial amount of common equity protecting the preferred shares. Generally speaking, the common equity absorbs losses before the preferred shareholders. The bigger that cushion, the better.

For most of the preferred shares we cover, this ratio is substantially higher. That's especially true for preferred shares with our lowest risk ratings.

It has been revealed that as an example, we recently covered DX-D (DX.PR.D) from Dynex Capital (DX). Dynex preferred shares have a coverage ratio around 11. Remember, MITT preferred shares have a ratio of 0.95.

One of these preferred shares has enough cushion to survive a fall from a roof.

The other is hoping gravity gets distracted.

MITT-B is offering investors a stripped yield around 12.10% and is in our buy range.

Industry observers note that however, MITT-B carries our highest risk rating. The weak coverage ratio is a large part of that. We believe there are other preferred shares presently trading at a much better risk/reward profile. For investors with a high-risk tolerance, MITT-B is worth considering.

Everyone would love a 12% yield from a preferred share issued by Dynex Capital or Annaly Capital.

MITT-B offers the yield but comes with our highest risk rating.
