I recently completed three of the top Christian financial education programs for churches: SeedTime’s True Financial Freedom, Dave Ramsey’s Financial Peace University, and Crown Financial’s MoneyLife.

These popular programs all claim to help you get control of your finances from a biblical perspective. However, they go about it in different ways with varying teaching styles and philosophies.

In this post, I’ll provide an in-depth look at each program – breaking down the unique features, strengths, weaknesses, and what’s actually included when you buy in.

My goal is to give you the real deal on these courses so you can determine which one (if any) is the best fit for transforming your financial life in a way that aligns with your faith. Whether you’re deep in debt, building wealth, or simply trying to honor God with your money, this comparison will help guide your journey.

Let’s dive into the nitty-gritty details of each program:.

It has been revealed that when it comes to pricing, Financial Peace University from Dave Ramsey sits in the middle. For an individual membership, it’s $69.99. They also offer bulk pricing for churches starting at around $800 for 10 memberships.

On the higher end, Seedtime’s True Financial Freedom charges $149 for an individual/couple license with regular deals making it available as low as $74. But they have some solid deals for Churches – you can get a bulk student license for as low as $48 per person if you buy multiple licenses. Or there’s an annual church subscription starting as low as $750 per year based on average attendance.

The most affordable option is Crown Financial’s MoneyLife course at just $29.95 for an individual purchase. I couldn’t find any publicly listed bulk pricing for churches, but being a non-profit, I’d expect them to be the cheapest route for congregations.

But as you’ll see, there are plenty more differences beyond just the price tags when comparing what’s actually included in each program.

True Financial Freedom, created by Bob Lotich and his wife Linda from SeedTime, is a financial literacy video course designed for churches that strikes a beautiful balance between biblical wisdom and practical money management strategies. The program’s goal is to equip Christians with the tools and mindset they need to experience true financial freedom while making an eternal impact for God’s Kingdom.

One of the standout features of True Financial Freedom is the engaging and relatable teaching style of Bob and Linda. They share their own financial struggles and triumphs with humor, transparency, and grace, making participants feel like they’re learning from wise, caring friends rather than aloof experts. This approach creates a safe, non-judgmental environment where participants can openly discuss their financial challenges and celebrate their progress.

The program offers several unique benefits, such as the “Never 100” rule (their ‘done-is-better-than-perfect’ approach to adjust spending) and the “Straight A” strategy for automating finances. These concepts are not only memorable but also highly actionable in helping participants take control of their money and build lasting wealth.

Recent findings suggest that another strength of True Financial Freedom is its emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy. Through interactive workshops, participants are guided in developing a custom blueprint that fits their unique situation, goals, and values. This approach recognizes that there’s no one-size-fits-all solution to personal finance and empowers participants to take ownership of their financial journey.

True Financial Freedom is perfect for Christians who want to learn how to thrive financially while staying grounded in the Bible. The program teaches participants how to avoid the extremes of being “so heavenly-minded they’re no earthly good” or becoming so focused on building worldly wealth that they lose sight of what truly matters.

With its grace-filled approach and practical tools, True Financial Freedom helps Christians find the balance needed to change their financial life and make a lasting difference in the world in the process.

Financial Peace University, created by Dave Ramsey and his team at Ramsey Solutions, is a highly popular financial education program that has helped countless individuals and families get out of debt and build wealth. The program’s primary goal is to guide participants through a proven, step-by-step approach to taking control of their money and achieving financial peace.

According to recent reports, dave Ramsey, the face of Financial Peace University, is known for his high-energy, tough love teaching style. He delivers hard-hitting truths about money with a sense of urgency and conviction that inspires participants to take action. However, some may find his approach a bit intense or even abrasive at times, likening it to going through bootcamp. While this style resonates with some, it may not be everyone’s preferred learning environment.

Recent findings suggest that the cornerstone of Financial Peace University is the “Baby Steps” system, a clear, prescriptive initiative for getting out of debt and building wealth. The program heavily emphasizes the debt snowball method, which involves paying off debts from smallest to largest, regardless of interest rates. This approach has proven highly effective in keeping participants motivated and helping them experience quick wins on their debt-free journey.

While Financial Peace University does incorporate some biblical principles, its overall approach is more secular in nature. The program focuses primarily on the practical nuts and bolts of money management, with less emphasis on exploring the deeper spiritual implications of financial stewardship.

Sources indicate that financial Peace University is best suited for individuals and families who are drowning in debt and need a clear, actionable plan to get back on track. The program’s structured approach and intense motivation can be a lifeline for those feeling overwhelmed by their financial situation. However, those seeking a more personalized, grace-filled approach that deeply integrates biblical wisdom may find other programs more appealing.

MoneyLife, offered by Crown Financial, is a financial education program that takes a deeply biblical approach to money management. The program’s primary goal is to guide Christians in understanding and applying God’s financial principles to their lives, emphasizing the importance of seeing God as the ultimate provider and owner of all resources.

One of MoneyLife’s distinguishing features is its strong focus on biblical teachings and spiritual practices related to money. The program dives deep into exploring how our financial decisions can reflect our faith and values, encouraging participants to align their money management with biblical principles. This emphasis on the spiritual aspects of finance sets MoneyLife apart from other programs that may focus more heavily on practical strategies.

According to recent reports, the teaching style in MoneyLife tends to be more academic and classroom-like compared to other programs. Participants can expect a significant amount of reading materials and written assessments throughout the course. While this approach may appeal to those who prefer a studious learning environment, it may not be as engaging for individuals who thrive on interactive, video-based content.

It has been revealed that moneyLife offers some unique elements, such as personality assessments that help participants understand how their natural tendencies impact their financial decisions. The program also includes exercises like the transfer of ownership, which guides participants in acknowledging God’s ultimate ownership of their resources. These introspective activities can be powerful tools for reshaping participants’ mindsets and habits around money.

However, one potential drawback of MoneyLife is that its emphasis on biblical principles and spiritual practices may come at the expense of providing highly actionable, practical financial strategies.

It has been revealed that moneyLife is ideal for Christians who are seeking a deeply biblical understanding of money management and are willing to engage in a more studious, reflective learning process. The program is well-suited for those who want to explore the spiritual foundations of financial stewardship and align their money habits with their faith. However, those primarily looking for a simple and easy financial strategy or a more interactive learning experience may find other programs that better fit their needs.

Having gone through all 3 programs, here is my personal experience and recommendations:.

In a recent development, I can honestly say that True Financial Freedom was a life-changing experience. Bob and Linda’s warm, relatable teaching style made me feel like I was learning from trusted friends who truly cared about my success. The program’s emphasis on creating a personalized financial strategy was a game-changer for me, as it helped me develop a plan that fit my unique situation and goals.

Personally, True Financial Freedom struck that balance better than any of the other programs on the list and gave me the strategy to move forward. My savings, giving, and earning have all increased in significant ways since taking the program.

Industry observers note that for those who are drowning in debt and need a clear, structured plan to get out, I highly recommend Financial Peace University. Dave Ramsey’s no-nonsense approach and the step-by-step “Baby Steps” system can provide the motivation and direction needed to tackle debt head-on. The debt snowball method, in particular, has helped countless people experience quick wins and build momentum on their debt-free journey. Just be prepared for a more intense, boot camp-style learning environment.

If you’re seeking a program that deeply explores the biblical principles behind money management, Crown’s MoneyLife might be the right fit for you. The program’s emphasis on spiritual practices and aligning your finances with your faith can be incredibly powerful for those who want to grow in their understanding of God’s perspective on wealth. However, be prepared for a more academic, reading-intensive learning experience and less focus on highly practical, actionable strategies.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the best program for you will depend on your unique financial situation, learning style, and personal goals. If you’re looking for a grace-filled, practical approach that helps you thrive in God’s Kingdom while making an eternal impact, I highly recommend True Financial Freedom. If you need a structured, intensive strategy to get out of debt fast, Financial Peace University could be your best bet. And if you desire a deep dive into the biblical foundations of money management, MoneyLife is worth considering.

Regardless of which program you choose, the most key thing is to take action and invest in your financial education. By doing so, you’ll be better equipped to handle the resources God has entrusted to you and experience the joy and freedom that comes from aligning your finances with your faith.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River.
  • This won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river.
  • Bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River. He set off on a homemade on a bamboo raft from the Dhola–Sadiya Bridge on November 1 and aims to finish at Dhubri, 891km later. The route covers the entire Brahmaputra within India and should take 22 to 25 days in all. The river begins in Tibet and continues beyond India into Bangladesh, covering 2,900km in all.

This won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river. In 2020, he and two friends took a similar bamboo raft down a 400km section of the Brahmaputra. Earlier, in 2015, Bordoloi was one of 11 who tackled another part of the river over 11 days under the auspices of the Assam Mountaineering Association. This expedition, however, will test his endurance, pitting him against river conditions for longer, and with less support, than ever before.

Bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra. This raft took Bordoloi and friends from the world’s largest river island, Umananda, to its smallest, Majuli. Photo: Shekhar Bordoloi/Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that bordoloi’s raft was hand-built from bamboo poles carefully lashed together over several days. Such craft are a traditional way of navigating rivers across the region, and are still used by local communities for fishing and transportation.

Though the river can be temperamental, Bordoloi’s first two days have been relatively calm, taking him down the Lohit, one of the Brahmaputra’s many tributaries and channels. Navigating the complex river system alone will be a challenge. The Brahmaputra is one of the largest river systems in India, the ninth-largest in the world by discharge, and is prone to flooding and powerful currents.

Industry observers note that but according to Bordoloi, those obscure, winding corridors are at the heart of this project. Many sections of the river remain underexplored, and he believes there is hidden potential for the people in his home region of Assam. If he can map routes for river tourism and model environmentally responsible river navigation through those routes, he hopes to draw attention to this important riverine ecosystem and the economic opportunities for the people living along it.

Recent findings suggest that the logistical challenges of a long expedition will further complicate progress. On previous expeditions, Bordoloi traveled with minimal supplies or no food at all, relying entirely on foraging and knowledge of the natural landscape. But this adventure will take over twice as long and may put those skills to their limits.

Bordoloi is documenting his daily progress on Facebook and Instagram.

Details, Video of Jugal II First Ascent

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route.
  • The peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023.
  • Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route. Yet, the climbers insist that the best part of the experience was climbing part of the route with Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet. Jugal II was Proposal B for the Italian pair after flooding washed out access to their primary target, Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region.

The peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023. In the end, it was the skill and smart strategy of Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain that put them on the unclimbed 6,518m summit after an alpine-style push via the east-southeast face.

Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.

The team said that the greatest technical difficulties came high on the route. “From the upper bivouac, the climb goes on pretty vertical mixed terrain, with sections of poor-quality rock,” Zabalza explained. “It’s sustained M5 with some even harder sections, until 6,450m. Then the rest of the way to the summit follows along a 55˚-60˚snow slope.”.

Recent findings suggest that A tough, vertical mixed section. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

In a recent development, they reached the summit on October 29, at 4:00 pm. The weather was clear but very cold, with some evening humidity.

According to recent reports, “We made three bivouacs on the route, two on the way up and one more on descent, and all of them were rather precarious,” Mikel Zabalza told ExplorersWeb from Kathmandu. “Luckily, we had a tarp to enlarge them.”.

Sources indicate that one of the climbers on the summit of Jugal II. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

In a recent development, the Spanish team, all highly experienced alpinists, had been studying the route for months. This was key to their success.

The situation was different for Benet and Meroi of Italy. Since they had not planned to do Jugal II, their approach to the route was more improvisational. They had no previous information about what they would find. To make matters worse, the third member of the team, Tine Cuder of Slovenia, had to abandon the expedition due to health problems.

Industry observers note that one of the Spanish team’s bivouacs, with a tiny ledge enlarged by a fabric tarp. Photo: Romano Benet.

Industry observers note that there was no competition between the two teams, who happily joined forces for the summit push. However, the Spaniards’ strategy proved essential on the highly steep ramps covered with unstable snow.

Nivel Meroi loaded with bivy gear on highly steep mixed ramps on Jugal II. Photo: Romano Benet.

Industry observers note that “We set off on an adventure, having never seen the mountain before and not knowing what kind of ascent awaited us, but we gave it a try,” Romano Benet reported from Kathmandu. “We decided to turn back to avoid a third bivouac. ”.

The two teams joined forces and were in good spirits on the route. Photo: Romano Benet.

Benet explained that they lacked the necessary gear (specifically, a tarp like Zabalza’s group) to pitch bivvies “on this type of face, where it’s impossible to carve out a ledge.”.

It has been revealed that otherwise, the two groups returned as friends. “Nives and Romano are exceptional people,” Zabalza said.

“We are back from the mountain with new experiences and ideas but, most of all, with three new fantastic friends with whom, hopefully, we will share more adventures in the future,” Romano Benet concluded.

The Spanish team sent us the video below summarizing the climb.

Breaking: Huge Crowds Trek to Everest Base Camp

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (544 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the image of an endless line of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp this week seemed like deja vu.
  • Ngima Sherpa of Osprey Adventure explained that this is not the norm, but the delay caused by Cyclone Anwar, which hit Nepal last weekend, has created a huge backlog.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the image of an endless line of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp this week seemed like deja vu. Why are conga lines similar to the infamous ones filmed every May on Everest’s Hillary Step, now repeating at the base of the mountain? We asked the local trekking guide who shot the video.

Ngima Sherpa of Osprey Adventure explained that this is not the norm, but the delay caused by Cyclone Anwar, which hit Nepal last weekend, has created a huge backlog.

Recent findings suggest that “Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained. “This video was shot on November 1, after three days of continuous snow and rain…During that time, all the trekkers were stuck in Dingboche, which is two trekking stages away from Everest Base Camp.”.

When the weather finally cleared, all those trekkers set off for EBC at the same time, causing heavy traffic on the route from Dingboche to Gorakshep.

The recent cyclone is also the reason why the surroundings are so heavily covered in snow. Usually, the entire trail to Everest Base Camp is dry.

The fresh snow on Nepal’s peaks is having consequences for those planning to summit trekking peaks. Conditions on otherwise straightforward snow slopes have become problematic, as climbers sink into deep, heavy snow.

Industry observers note that satori Adventures had to retreat after swimming in snow on the flanks of Mera Peak, in the Khumbu. “Four to five feet of fresh snow made it impossible to move forward above high camp,” leader Furba Sherpa reported.

Sources indicate that ramesh Gurung noted today that he has retreated from an attempt on 6,119m Lobuche East, another popular Khumbu 6000’er. However, Gurung said he will try again with another group soon.

Conditions will change only as the snow transforms under the dimming sun and freezes in the approaching winter temperatures.

According to recent reports, on Ama Dablam, Sherpa climbers struggled to reopen the route to Camp 1 on Tuesday but managed to complete it. The route above Camp 1 follows a steep, mixed ridge with less accumulated snow. Several teams are now on their summit rotations and expect to top out in the next few days.

Industry observers note that tenzing Sherpa of Gokyo Namaste Lodge has shared some useful information for trekkers who proposal to cross the huge Ngozumpa Glacier between Gokyo and Dragnag. The recent snowfall makes the usual route less safe, and he recommends following local people along an easier route between Longbanga Tso (1st Lake) and Taujung Tso (2nd Lake). See Tenzing’s sketch of the route:.

Alternative route between Gokyo Lakes, suggested by Gokyo Tenzing Sherpa.

Sources indicate that tenzing also noted that the route from Thame to Gokyo is open, as the Gokyo Lodge Association cleared and reopened the trail from the Gokyo side yesterday. However, conditions on the glacier may change rapidly.

The route across Gokyo is one of the most popular side trips in the Khumbu, for those wanting to enrich their Everest Base Camp trek. The area features stunning scenery, with high mountain lakes, glaciers, and a view of the formidable South Face of Cho Oyu.

Join Shell Fuel Rewards if most of your gas comes from Shell, since the free program takes 5 cents a gallon off every fill-up for drivers who buy 10 gallons or more there six times a quarter. When another station on your route undercuts your Shell by more than your discount, fill up there instead.

For an average car or SUV buying all its gas at Shell, those 5 cents a gallon come to about $21 a year on the 423 gallons it burns, by the Federal Highway Administration’s count. Industry observers note that drivers who already buy 10 gallons or more at Shell six times a quarter get the program’s 5 cents a gallon for nothing. Drivers without a Shell on their routes should check a gas price app and fill up at the cheapest station instead.

#9269. Will the AI Bubble Destroy our Retirement?

📅 25 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3279 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mrmoneymustache ↗ Open Full Page

Will the AI Bubble Destroy our Retirement?

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a phrase we keep having to dust off and use again, as the years go by and the market keeps surprising us.
  • When it crashes, some of us worry because we see our retirement stash shrinking.
  • But even when it rises to record levels and then to super-duper-crazy record valuations, we find reason to worry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wow, how about that stock market?

It’s a phrase we keep having to dust off and use again, as the years go by and the market keeps surprising us.

When it crashes, some of us worry because we see our retirement stash shrinking.

But even when it rises to record levels and then to super-duper-crazy record valuations, we find reason to worry. Because that just means an even bigger crash is coming, right? Especially when this boom-bubble is built on the back of something as frenzied as the present Artificial Intelligence boom… right?

According to recent reports, for those who have been happily tuned out of this drama and just enjoying life: Congratulations! Keep up the great work. But just to give you a quick background for the purposes of this article, here’s the AI story in three points:.

It has been revealed that investors worry that while AI is definitely a major invention, the mania around it is still too much, too fast, and thus we are due for an even bigger version of the dot com crash we had in the early 2000s. Which happens to be an interesting subject for me, since that was the boom that boosted my own early career and got me on the path to early retirement … before the ensuing crash almost cost me my job and my citizenship application.

Sources indicate that as an aging Internet Financial Guru, I have the privilege of getting lots of questions about this investment cycle, just as I have about past booms and busts. And to address them, I decided to not only write this blog article but also create a little talk about it – which I already gave for the first time at an event called Camp FI Midwest earlier this month. I also hope to polish it up and deliver an improved version at the Bogleheads conference in November.

So what that means is that today you not only get a blog post, but a few silly presentation slides to go with it for extra entertainment. All with no need for a plane ticket or all that hassle of leaving your house. So let’s get into it!

It has been revealed that so I recently hit 21 years of retirement. This means I’ve grown pretty comfortable with the idea. But it still threw me for a loop one time when a friend asked me this question:.

Recent findings suggest that “How can you be retired, and comfortable in your retirement, and sleep at night, with everything that’s going on in the world? Aren’t you worried?”.

And I was like, “No, what should I be worried about?”.

Sources indicate that but if you’re a news watcher and a worrier yourself, you can probably think of a few things I should be worried about. Perhaps stuff like this:.

You’ve got our corrupt and/or dangerous politicians like Trump and Putin menacing the world. Inflation eroding our purchasing power, the AI Bubble, the towering US National Debt, the Iran war and the Ukraine war and all these other wars that are just on the verge of tipping us all into destruction.

But it turns out these were not the things my friend was asking about.

Because she actually asked me this question over twenty years ago… In the year 2006. So back then we were worried about entirely different things, right?

Recent findings suggest that back then we had corrupt and/or dangerous leaders like Bush, Hussein and of course Bin Laden. There was still a war in the middle east but it was Iraq instead of Iran. We were still worried about the National Debt and Inflation. And we also worried about our overvalued stock market. But back then it was because of the housing bubble instead of the AI bubble. And instead of AI taking our jobs it was going to be outsourcing to India and China.

Oh and here’s an interesting one: There was a big debate over Peak Oil, and whether the world was doomed because fossil fuel use was always increasing while supply was bound to decrease. And it turns out the opposite happened as you’ll see below.

So then after all this worry in 2006, what ended up happening?

Well we did get the Great Financial Crisis, which was caused by a combination of irrational exuberance over increasing house prices combined with a foolish degree of fancy leverage in the financial instruments used to issue mortgages. And it was the biggest crash since the Great Depression.

Industry observers note that but even in that craziest of situations, look how minor it looks in the substantial picture. A $100,000 investment still ended up ballooning into $852,000 today. And if you look carefully in here you can just see the Covid Crash tucked in there in 2020. Remember that?

And not only that, the rest of the world got a lot better too:.

In a recent development, the portion of people living in extreme poverty dropped from 20% in 2005 to only 8% over the next 20 years. Infant mortality – children who die in their first year of life – was cut in half. Clean energy became a thing as solar panels became about 40 times cheaper. So solar generation now makes up the vast majority of all the new generation we add today (the equivalent of 647 nuclear power plants of peak capacity added last year, but with much cheaper and easier solar panels). And sales of pure electric cars have gone from zero up to about a quarter of all the cars sold on Earth last year, on its way to 100%, which is where they already are in Norway.

So if we circle back to that question my friend asked me 20 years ago: do you think I should have focused my energy on worrying about an uncertain future, or optimism?

Which of course brings up the question: Is it different this time?

It has been revealed that maybe the US national debt is finally substantial enough to really start messing with us. Maybe the AI bubble is way bigger than the housing bubble and we won’t bounce back from this next stock market crash. Or maybe AI will spin out of control into a super intelligence that takes over the planet and realizes it does not need us any more.

It has been revealed that and the financial media loves to spin a good scary story about all of this. But you know what the fear mongers all seem to be missing?

It’s the fact that at the core, our prosperity does not come from the financial system or the stock market, which are just some made-up numbers on some computers.

Really, Prosperity comes from Productivity.

Recent findings suggest that we first covered this lesson right here on MMM, in the 2014 Classic entitled, “Why we are not really all doomed”. And sure enough, twelve years later the timeless lessons therein remain just as true now as they were back then.

It has been revealed that and the lesson is really simple: the world of capitalism is always choppy and prone to wild swings. But if you peek beneath the waves, there are real people in there, doing real work and coming up with real inventions.

In fact, the very idea of an “economy” or a financial system is just another human invention. If the whole system crashes because we don’t like the numbers we see in there, we can literally make up some fresh numbers and then get back to work. Which is exactly what we did in 2008 and many times before that, and it seems to have worked just fine.

Meanwhile, we still have every tool we ever invented to boost our productivity. And our standard of living, and our economic growth, and our possibility of retiring early, all come from high productivity.

But even Productivity and Prosperity aren’t all that important.

Because once we reach a certain standard of living, human happiness kind of tops out in that dimension. In first-world countries, we blew past those minimum requirements several decades ago. And then we start looking for other factors to maximize our overall happiness. All anybody really wants is to lead the happiest, most satisfying life they can manage.

And when you think of it that way, your wealth is really just part of your life situation, which is part of this little green slice of the happiness pie.

It has been revealed that genetics is unfortunately the biggest slice – some people are just plain happier than others. But there are also quite a few choices that are within your control.

Focusing on good close relationships and being kind to people. Practicing Gratitude and Optimism as your lifelong philosophy. And making sure you pack as many healthy (outdoor) activities into your days as you can.

According to recent reports, so, I didn’t invent anything new in this blog post. And most of it is just a repackaging of the same stuff I’ve been writing about since 2011. And yet some regular MMM readers who presumably know all this stuff are STILL afraid. Afraid to retire, afraid of things in their unknown future. Can we fix this?

I think the biggest problem is Fear Itself.

Sources indicate that the problem is that as a Human Being, you are basically a Danger Detection Machine. And this pervasive background fear is just a trait we evolved to protect ourselves from danger.

But there’s a weird thing about our detection machinery. We can adapt and learn to function even in very dangerous environments, but when the danger goes away, we keep looking for stuff to worry about. In other words, there is a problem with fear: for many of us, it never really goes away. It just keeps moving the goalposts.

While Nature has wisely endowed us with a fear of predators and disease, if you solve those things you’ll just start worrying about whether or not you can get enough food. And supplies, and protecting yourself against scarcity.

If you succeed, next you’ll be worrying about if you can fit in with your tribe, because if you don’t, you might be exiled.

In a recent development, and if you don’t have to worry about that, you’ll go back to worrying about money for different reasons. Thanks to our tendency to use comparisons rather than absolutes (sometimes called “anchoring bias” and the “contrast effect”) when judging our lives, just getting out of poverty isn’t enough. We just move on to wanting more money.

And then, when some people get enough money to have a comfortable upper-middle-class lifestyle, they take the logical next step of starting a Homeowner’s Association, so they can worry about the unauthorized weeds on their neighbor’s lawn. Or maybe a Political Action Committee in hopes of controlling the color of their future neighbors’ skin.

And even if all the lawns and gardens are green and perfect and people get really rich, they just move on to worry about tax strategy, leaving a huge inheritance for their children, and avoiding RMDs.

Required minimum Distributions. This is when, if you get to 75 years old and you have too much money, the government will start making you withdraw some of that money so you can spend it and pay taxes on it. And people actually worry about this. I shit you not.

But wait! You can actually fight back against fear. It’s just a bit tricky because it requires some self awareness. But you have the advantage, because you have the ability to think rationally. And your fear is quite clearly irrational.

And the first step is to understand your own history. Are you afraid of certain things because of your childhood?

I might have been afraid of running out of money, because in my family there was always a perceived shortage of the stuff, possibly enforced by my Dad’s scarcity mentality. And he was aware that his own fears of scarcity came from childhood as well: he grew up in a truly low income family in the 1940s and 50s, under the care of parents who had lived through the Great Depression of the 1930s.

Even more significant is that survivors of trauma and abuse will very likely end up with fear complications in adulthood. It’s natural, and unfortunately abuse is way more widespread even in this country than we would like to admit. This makes it harder to eliminate, but it still helps to understand that your past is what is causing these feelings, rather than an objective understanding of the present.

Identify the Fear: Once you understand yourself, it helps to talk through the nature of your fear in more detail. This is also often taught in therapy. What would happen if it really came true? What would the worst case scenario be? It’s often not all that bad.

In one post, why you’ll probably never run out of money, I went to great lengths to imagine what it would mean for a wealthy person like yourself to actually let the well run dry, and let’s say you’ll probably never come close.

It has been revealed that once you identify the fear, you can start taking action. And one of the best and most accurate slogans ever is that action cures fear. It’s because it makes the unfamiliar, familiar. And you get confidence that you can really create change. And then that learning creates Resilience – the ability to adapt to ANY new situation, which is a trait also known as Badassity. And with sufficient Badassity, nothing is scary.

Think about it: if you had the skills and abilities to handle ANY situation, skills in the mental and physical and even the realms of emotion and wisdom, would you really have to worry about anything?

The next thing you can do is tune out all the unnecessary crap from your daily mental diet. And for most Americans, this means the daily news.

The news is not helping you to keep informed, it’s just poisoning your mind with a hand-picked selection of the scariest stories of each day. If you want to learn about something, go find a book on the subject. And if you want to make a difference, the only thing that counts is not the news stories you watch – it’s only the actions that you take – in other words, your Positive Behaviors.

As a human being, you are wired to solve problems with both your body and your mind, and you are meant to do it outdoors. So if you spend all your days in a house and a car and in an office using the computer, of course you are going to have some mental health problems. This should not be a surprising thing you need to ask your therapist about, it is an expected result of not living the life that you were literally created to live as a Human being!

So you need to focus on learning, moving, and solving problems. And you need your food and drink intake to be in alignment with all of this too. Life will get a lot less scary as soon as you are living life in the way you were built to live it.

Then finally, you can start swapping out the fear-mongers in your life, for other positive, productive, optimistic people. And watch how much the positive mentality rubs off on you. In the FI community, at least the subgroup of people that I like to spend time with, nobody focuses on fear. It’s all just about living the best life we can, and helping other people do so as well.

So now that we know how to fight back against fear, we can start using a upcoming approach when we go into anything new. And that approach is something I like to call Everything is an Experiment.

It has been revealed that and this applies whether you are talking about something tiny like a newly introduced paint color. But it scales up to bigger things like switching to a new car, or a new house, meeting new friends, looking for new love by going through the sometimes hell of first dates, a new job, or even quitting your last job by taking an early retirement.

So let’s bring this back around to AI, the thing that everybody seems to be afraid of right now.

According to recent reports, I think of our newly introduced AI era as just being another giant experiment. And because of this, I don’t find it even remotely scary. But I do find it endlessly fascinating.

Recent findings suggest that first of all, it’s a change. A potentially unknown one, and for some people that’s scary.

Recent findings suggest that but instead of just leaving it there and then doom-scrolling ominous news articles about it, why not learn why people are so excited about AI? As someone with a lifelong background in technology and economics (and a general lack of political affiliation), I can see a lot more potential upside than downside. And that mainly comes from the fact that I see AI as just a very fancy form of Cognitive Nail Gun.

Recent findings suggest that it will boost our efficiency, which means our productivity, which means prosperity. Because it’s really just a super smart brain that we all get to tap into at a fairly negligible cost.

In a recent development, unfortunately, it will also displace workers like every other new productivity technology. It’s already doing so in things like entry level office jobs in software and finance. It will eventually replace car and truck drivers, and so on. But in exchange, these services will become cheaper, and new industries will be created because of the new technology. Much like the Internet itself, and then the enormous industries unleashed by smartphones and mobile apps.

It has been revealed that and one unfortunate side effect of these latest inventions is that they tend to concentrate their rewards on the people who own them. If you own a house building manufacturer and employ a bunch of carpenters and give nail guns to the best of those carpenters, you can now lay off the other half and still get more done. If you own a company and roll out AI to the workers, you can do the same thing.

And if you’re a big public company, your shareholders also benefit, which happens to include most of the people reading this. As you’ve seen when looking at your portfolios over the past two years.

Artificial Intelligence is just like any other newly introduced thing that pops into your life: it’s an opportunity to make some choices. And it is up to you to decide if this is something to be afraid of, or to use as a trigger for learning, action, and living a more interesting life.

So that’s my little talk (and surprisingly long blog post) on Fear versus the AI bubble.

I hope that if you do feel fearful about this or any other issue in your future life, you’ll take it as a cue to learn more about your own fear and emotions and manage them as the root cause they are, rather than just trying to avoid the symptoms. Because in the wise words of my friends The Donegans:.

Recent findings suggest that everything you want in life, that you don’t already have,lies on the other side of Fear. Because if you weren’t afraid to go out there and get it, you would already have it.

Animal Attack Roundup, Nov. 4

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife.
  • As expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts.
  • Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife. People who live and work every day among animals are the ones who most often face the consequences.

As expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts. Here are some recent incidents.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.

In Indonesia, 24-year-old Selviana Ambu Kaka was attacked by a crocodile while washing clothes in the Bondo Kodi River. Her fiancé and his sister witnessed a large crocodile emerging from the water, biting Ambu Kaka on the leg, and dragging her into the river. They immediately alerted nearby relatives and authorities, and a search commenced.

The people of Southwest Sumba, the closest town, organized and combed the area with nets. When they found a large crocodile matching witness descriptions, they hauled it onto shore and killed it. The animal measured nearly 4.9 meters long.

Early on the morning of October 24, Ambu Kaka’s remains were found approximately 30m from the attack site. She is one of many such victims in Indonesia, which sees more saltwater crocodile attacks than any other country.

Sources indicate that habitat destruction is largely behind the massive number of human-crocodile conflicts. It’s an understandably hard sell, however, for conservation workers to convince locals that preventing attacks means protecting the perpetrators.

The victim had recently returned from Jakarta to become formally engaged on October 30.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/ Rohit Gangwal, CC BY-SA 4.0.

Sources indicate that A 65-year-old farm laborer, Tulsi Rama Sawar, was killed by a leopard in state of Maharashtra, just north of Mumbai, on November 1. The noise of the attack summoned help from the locals. By the time they arrived, the leopard had fled, but Sawar was deceased. Her case comes less than a month after a leopard killed a 52-year-old woman in the same area.

Industry observers note that town residents are demanding immediate government action to capture the animal. If their demands for cage traps and cameras are not granted, locals threaten collective protest. The attacks represent a threat to their lives, but also their livelihoods, as farmers are unable to work the fields out of fear of attack.

In a recent development, elsewhere, in Uttar Pradesh near the Nepal border, a 45-year-old farmer named Kennu fought off an attacking leopard, sustaining serious injuries. The man was working in a sugarcane field when the predator leaped out from hiding. Kennu fought back, and the animal retreated long enough for him to flee home, where family members brought him to medical care. Forestry officials have urged agricultural workers to avoid working in the fields alone.

In a recent development, farm workers are not the only leopard victims, however. Early in the morning of November 4, a 15-year-old girl was dragged from her home in the Shahdol district of central India.

In a recent development, saraswati Singh Gond was sleeping in bed beside her sister on their veranda, which did not have a door. A leopard entered during the night, not even waking her sister. Singh Gond’s body was found approximately 300m from the house. The search for the leopard continues.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Shadow Ayush, CC BY-SA 4.0.

Leopards are only one of the wildlife threats that rural Indians face. A 55-year-old woman was gathering mushrooms in Utterakand in northern India on October 30 when she was attacked and killed by a wild elephant. Devaki Rana was lifted up and thrown to the ground, her son reported.

Industry observers note that the incident occurred in one of India’s elephant corridors, which allow highly endangered Asian elephant herds to move between their fragmented habitats. The corridors are essential to conservation, but also present a concentrated area where attacks are more common.

In a recent development, another fatal encounter took place in the state of Chhattisgarh in east-central India. A man of between 35 and 40 years of age, traveling by motorcycle with his nephew, came upon an elephant standing in the road. It immediately charged them, killing the uncle, while his nephew managed to hide beneath a parked truck. Eventually, the elephant left, and he was able to escape.

Locals believe that the elephant in question is one known as Kabra Kaan, which they see frequently and which has been connected with earlier incidents. The Forestry Department, however, has not confirmed this.

Sources indicate that elephant corridors allow them to pass between the remaining forested areas. Photo: Wildlife Trust of India.

In Japan, brown bear attacks have been rising for several years. As in many places, human settlements are encroaching on brown bear territory. A decrease in farmland has left no boundary between the urban and the forested worlds. The government has responded with controversial bear culls, despite the concerns of conservation workers.

In a recent development, the latest incident is very different from the increasingly common attack stories. Late on the night of October 30, an express train running on Hokkaido’s Soya Line collided with a large brown bear. The body of the bear was trapped under the train, and the wheels derailed.

A brown bear became trapped beneath the wheels of Sarobetsu No 3. Photo: Hokkaido Railway Tech giant.

None of the crew or 32 passengers were injured in the crash. However, fearing more bears were in the area, officials kept everyone on the train overnight, until they could be safely extracted the following morning. Company officials have confirmed that this is the first bear-collision derailment in their nearly 40-year history.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Find the cheapest gas station on your route with GasBuddy’s free price map, then trim what you pay there. Claim an Upside offer if the station takes part, use Checkout 51 if you already scan grocery receipts in it, and join Shell Fuel Rewards if Shell is your usual stop.

It has been revealed that the two steps work together because gas apps do different jobs. Each pick here does one of them best for a particular driver. A price map demonstrates the prices drivers report at nearby stations, so you can compare stations before you fill up and pick the cheapest one on your route. The other apps cut what you pay at the station you choose, with cash back on an offer you claim before you pump or a discount at one brand’s stations.

Sources indicate that an average car or SUV burned 423 gallons in 2024, by the Federal Highway Administration’s count. That makes every 5 cents off a gallon worth about $21 a year. Claim one cash back offer per fill-up, since Upside pays nothing on a fill-up that Checkout 51 or GasBuddy already paid cash back on.

Check its map before you claim a cash back offer, since a station with no offer can still cost less than one with an offer, even counting the cash back.

For more information, read our full GasBuddy Review.

Commuters who pass several participating stations do best with it, since each station funds its own offer and the app demonstrates every offer nearby before you pump.

For more information, read our full Upside Review.

It belongs here for drivers who already upload grocery receipts to it, since they can claim its gas offers without adding another app.

For more information, read our full Checkout 51 Review.

Drivers who buy 10 gallons or more at Shell about twice a month keep its 5-cent Gold discount, which still applies with an Upside offer, though Upside may trim that offer.

For more information, read our full Shell Fuel Rewards Review.

In a recent development, checking prices saves money before you choose a station, and a cash back offer or a loyalty discount adds to those savings once you’re there. Before each fill-up, open the price map, then claim an offer or enter your loyalty number at the station you pick.

For a card that earns on every fill-up, compare the best gas credit cards.
